note: What a screen says, unasked, about a translation — the corner notification, whole: whether it shows, what it says, what its one button does, and, when somebody else's lineage is offered the choice between contributing and forking, which door is open and why the other is not. Most urgent first: a conflict, a version waiting on the site, one waiting upstream, this machine's unsent lines, its unsent settings, contributions waiting on a Main. A username travels apart from the sentence; a wall already names somebody and is written as it is.

sync.in: the fact sheets of standing/from (with lines_changed: how many lines the published copy changed, and lines_changed_here: how many lines here differ from it — both null until the client counted, and the mod's own local_changes stands in for the second), plus what is waiting: waiting_for_account, has_local_changes, has_metadata_changes, has_server_update, needs_merge, has_main_update (bools), branches_pending_review (int)
sync.out: {show, message, mention, action, verb, offers_branch, branch_closed, fork_closed, wall} — compared on the keys the case names

cases.why: a notification with nothing to say is noise
🔴 the public endpoint fills the state with 'not the owner'; read before the account's own check answered, it offered the OWNER the two buttons meant for a stranger

out.message: Changed here (3) and on the site. Sync needed.

cases.why: both sides moved: this one always speaks up, and first; how many lines here is known, how many there is not yet

out.message: Changed here (2) and on the site (3). Sync needed.

cases.why: what changes, on both sides, before deciding — the site only says that it moved, the client counted from the copy it fetched; four lines changed here since the sync, but two of them the site also has, identically, so two differ — the same numbers the comparison page will show
who moved is named, apart from the sentence
Main or branch alike, it is THEIR OWN published version that moved — another machine, or the site editor; this used to claim a parent update for a branch, naming the wrong source

out.message: Update available on the site (5 lines).

cases.why: the published version moved and nothing did here: taken in whole, once the count is known or not
taking it costs nothing
a different exchange from a server update: it is merged into the branch, never downloaded over it
the count stays inline: the interface's translation placeholders numbers, so every count shares one cache entry

out.message: 3 local changes and settings to upload.

cases.why: lines and settings both unsent are said together: an exclusion added behind three lines went unsaid, and the person could not know an upload was owed for it
contribute (branch) or go independent (fork): a choice, never an act taken for them
🔴 the refusal is said before the click; a fork asks for neither the network nor an account and stays open precisely when the other door is shut

out.wall: @alice works alone on this one and does not take contributions. Fork keeps your lines as your own version.

cases.why: absent rather than greyed: a lineage that refuses contributions is not a 'later', it is a road that does not exist — the wall says which one, in the socle's words

out.message: Translation settings changed — not uploaded yet

cases.why: settings that travel with the translation are work not yet sent

out.message: You changed translation settings. Share them?

cases.why: same choice, said for settings
last, and rightly so: nothing degrades while it waits — but a contribution nobody hears about is a contributor lost
most urgent first: work at risk before work waiting

🔴 the one state with NO row on the site: every other branch compares two sides and this one has a single side, so each of them asked 'does it exist on the server' and fell silent — a translation could grow for a hundred hours unmentioned
publishing needs an account, and the person most likely to sit on unpublished work is the one who never made one: a door rather than the wall ClosedReason would have raised
having no row on the site is not a reason to interrupt anybody; whether there is enough here is measured by the caller (Quality.Completeness against TranslationFloor) and arrives as the flag
